{{ElectionsNV}}

The '''2026 Nevada gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Nevada]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Joe Lombardo]] is seeking a second term. He is being challenged by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] attorney general [[Aaron Ford (Nevada politician)|Aaron Ford]]. 

[[Primary elections]] took place on June 9, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 9, 2025|title=2026 State Primary Election Dates|url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|website=[[National Conference of State Legislatures]]|access-date=August 5, 2025}}</ref> Lombardo won the Republican nomination with 91.0% of the vote. Ford won the Democratic nomination with 63.8% over Washoe commission chair [[Alexis Hill (Nevada politician)|Alexis Hill]].

== Background ==
Nevada is considered to be a purple to slightly blue state at the federal and state levels, with neither party having [[Government trifecta|control of all three]] branches of government. Apart from the governor, Nevada's [[Lieutenant Governor of Nevada|lieutenant governor]] and [[Nevada State Controller|state controller]] are Republicans. Nevada's [[Nevada Attorney General|attorney general]], [[Nevada State Treasurer|treasurer]], and [[Secretary of State of Nevada|state secretary of state]] are Democrats.{{cn|date=March 2026}} [[Donald Trump]] won the state in [[2024 United States presidential election|2024]], becoming the first Republican presidential nominee to win the state since [[2004 United States presidential election in Nevada|2004]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Trump turns Nevada red in presidential race for first time in two decades |url=https://abc3340.com/news/nation-world/trump-turns-nevada-red-in-presidential-race-for-first-time-in-two-decades |access-date=March 6, 2026 |publisher=ABC3340 |date=November 6, 2024}}</ref>

The [[Nevada Legislature]] is controlled by members of the Democratic Party, with a majority in both the [[Nevada Assembly|state assembly]] and [[Nevada Senate|senate]]. The lieutenant governor, a Republican, serves as the president of the state senate but only votes in the case of a tie. At the federal level, both [[United States Senate|United States Senators]] and three out of four members of the [[United States House of Representatives]] from Nevada are Democrats.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Election Results, 2022 |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/election-results-2022/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221123004555/https://www.reviewjournal.com/election-results-2022/ |archive-date=November 23, 2022 |work=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Election Results, 2024 |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/general-election-results-2024/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241229090710/https://www.reviewjournal.com/general-election-results-2024/ |archive-date=December 29, 2024 |work=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]}}</ref>

With the exception of [[2018 Nevada gubernatorial election|2018]], Republicans have won every gubernatorial election in the state since [[1998 Nevada gubernatorial election|1998]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Mueller |first1=Tabitha |last2=Golonka |first2=Sean |last3=Solis |first3=Jacob |date=November 11, 2022 |title=Lombardo defeats Sisolak; Democrats win attorney general, secretary of state races |url=https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/lombardo-defeats-sisolak-democrats-win-attorney-general-secretary-of-state-races |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221112031753/https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/lombardo-defeats-sisolak-democrats-win-attorney-general-secretary-of-state-races |archive-date=November 12, 2022 |work=[[The Nevada Independent]]}}</ref>
